question: How do hyperscale software engineering and SRE organizations (Google SRE, Google DeepMind, AWS Chaos, Netflix Chaos Monkey, Meta, Palantir, OWASP, CNCF, SEI CMU, Gentleman/Engram) design adversarial engineering laboratories, hypothesis-driven chaos experimentation, steady-state baselines, blast radius control, and anti-self-deception protocols?
scope: Autonomous adversarial testing, failure injection taxonomy, 5-stage resilience model (Detect, Contain, Recover, Verify, Learn), 17-step Game Day state machine, blast radius limits (B0-B3), anti-self-deception validation, and proposal-only evolution
claims: EOS must treat the possibility of being wrong as a normal engineering condition.
Critical claims must be refutable via independent verification, rollback, and adversarial experimentation.
Chaos experiments must be hypothesis-driven with strict blast radius controls.
evidence: Netflix Chaos Automation Platform (ChAP) and AWS Resilience Hub enforce strict blast radius boundaries and steady-state invariant monitoring before injecting failure.
Google SRE DiRT (Disaster Recovery Testing) requires independent verifiers to confirm recovery without self-certification.
observations: Adversarial experiments must never mutate governance or release authority automatically; all learnings produce PROPOSAL_ONLY evolution candidates.
System resilience requires measuring Detection, Containment, Recovery, Verification, and Learning.
limitations: Adversarial laboratory operates locally in synthetic mode prior to live commercial infrastructure integration.
recommendation: Implement Adversarial Laboratory Engine, Adversarial Truth Principle, Attack Taxonomy, Blast Radius Model, Resilience Model, Game Day State Machine, Synthetic Adversarial Fixtures, and EVD-0021 in EOS Control Plane.
